action.failed_failed: That didn't work: the node may be busy or offline. Try again.
action.failed_invalid: The node can't use that address.
action.failed_no_key: Hub has no API key for this node.
action.failed_no_time_sync: The node's clock isn't synced yet. Try again in a minute.
action.failed_node_changed: Hub's API key is for another node. Choose this node again to give Hub its key.
action.failed_public: The public node takes no admin actions.

control.bootstrap_body: The node restarts, downloads a fresh copy of the chain and replaces its own. Use it when the node is stuck or far behind. It's offline for a while, and minting stops meanwhile.
control.bootstrap_done: The node is restarting to bootstrap.
control.bootstrap_not_back: The node stopped to bootstrap and hasn't come back.
control.bootstrap_still_up: The node hasn't restarted to bootstrap: it's still running as before. If Core's bootstrap failed, Core's own output may say why (its terminal, or run.log in its folder).
control.key_ok: Hub's API key for this node works.
control.log_note: The log can hold IP addresses and names. Check it before you share it.
control.restart_body: Restarts the node. It's offline for a minute or two, and minting pauses until it's back.
control.restart_not_back: The node stopped to restart and hasn't come back.
control.restart_still_up: The node hasn't restarted: it's still running as before. If Core's restart failed, Core's own output may say why (its terminal, or run.log in its folder).
control.start_body: Hub can start the node on this PC again.
control.start_done: Hub asked Core to start. The node takes a little while to answer.
control.start_elsewhere: Hub can only start Core from the folder it knows, and Core isn't there. Choose the folder your Core runs from (the one with qortal.jar), and Hub can start it.
control.start_failed: Core still isn't answering. If it doesn't start, start it the way you usually do.
control.start_still_running: Core is still running on this PC. Hub can start it again once it has stopped.
control.stop_body: Stops the node. Hub loses its connection to it, and minting stops, until it's started again.
control.support_body: A short summary of this node to paste into a help chat: versions, height, sync, peers, minting and memory. It holds no addresses, names, IPs or keys.

data.blocked_failed: Hub couldn't read the names your node blocks.
data.blocked_hint: Your node doesn't fetch or share files of the names it blocks, even names it follows. Unblock also unblocks the name's owner when their account is blocked too.
data.cant_remove_followed: Your node follows {{name}}, so Core would fetch a removed file straight back. Unfollow first to remove its files.
data.cant_remove_older: An older version. Core can remove only the newest version of a file.
data.cant_remove_own: You published this. Your node may hold the only copy, so it can't be removed here.
data.follow_body: Your node will fetch and share everything {{name}} publishes: {{size}} so far, and more as they publish. It stops fetching when its storage is 80 % full.
data.follow_body_at_least: Your node will fetch and share everything {{name}} publishes: at least {{size}} so far, and more as they publish. It stops fetching when its storage is 80 % full.
data.follow_body_unknown: Your node will fetch and share everything {{name}} publishes. It stops fetching when its storage is 80 % full.
data.followed_about: Your node keeps and shares the files of the names it follows, and fetches what they publish next.
data.gone_info: Its folder isn't on this PC any more. Core keeps listing the file until it counts its data again, about every two hours, or 10 minutes after Core starts.
data.name_none: Your node holds none of {{name}}'s files.
data.preview_build_needed: Your node holds this as parts. Showing it makes the node put together a full copy beside them: about {{size}} more on disk, which Core removes again an hour or more later.
data.preview_failed: Couldn't check what your node holds.
data.preview_none: No preview for this kind of data.
data.preview_older: Your node holds an older version: showing it would fetch the newest.
data.preview_partial: Your node holds only part of this: showing it would start a download.
data.preview_private: Encrypted: only its details show here.
data.remove_body: Your node deletes its copy of {{file}} ({{size}}) and stops sharing it. It fetches it again only if something on this node opens it.
data.remove_followed: Another list on your node (a Q-App's) still follows {{name}}, so Core would fetch this again: nothing was removed.
data.remove_not_removed: Core answered, but your node still holds part of this file.
data.remove_older: Core removes only the newest version of a file, and this one is older: nothing was removed.
data.remove_title: Remove this file from your node?
data.scan_partial: Only the first {{items}} items are sorted.
data.shared_snapshot: Core counts this list when it starts and then about every two hours, so it can be up to two hours old.
data.shared_totals: Your node shares {{items}} items, {{space}} on disk.
data.still_followed: {{name}} is off this list, but another list on your node (a Q-App's) still follows it.
data.unfollow_body: Your node stops fetching what {{name}} publishes. With Core's usual storage setting it keeps the files it already has and goes on sharing them.

peers.add_data_intro: Your node connects to this address for QDN data right away. Use a host name, an IPv4 address, or an IPv6 address in brackets, with a port after a colon.
peers.add_intro: Your node adds this address to the peers it knows and may connect to it. Use a host name, an IPv4 address, or an IPv6 address in brackets, with a port after a colon if it isn't the usual one.
peers.added_data: Your node added {{address}} for QDN data.
peers.address_invalid: That isn't an address the node can use.
peers.data_not_connected: Your node already knew {{address}}, but couldn't connect to it just now.
peers.force_sync_body: Only for a node that's stuck. Your node takes this peer's newest blocks in place of its own, even when its own chain is stronger, and keeps going until it's level. Pick a peer most others agree with. It can take a few minutes.
peers.forget_all_body: Your node clears its list of known peers and drops its connections, then finds peers again from its own defaults. For a node that keeps connecting to bad peers.
peers.forgot_all: Your node forgot its known peers.
peers.known_body: Peers your node knows of: {{known}}. It connects to some of them at a time.
peers.public_readonly: These are the public node's peers. Adding or removing peers needs your own node.
peers.remove_body: Your node disconnects from this peer and forgets it. Other peers may tell it about this address again later.

sync.nothing_to_do: Already level with this peer: nothing to sync.
